title: UNIT 3: FLUID MECHANICS
notes:
✓ Fluid mechanics → Deals with the behavior of liquids and gases, both at rest and in motion.

✓ A fluid cannot resist a sideways/shearing force continuously, so it flows.

title: 3.1 FLUID STATICS
notes:
✓ Fluid statics → The study of fluids at rest. There is no relative motion between adjacent fluid layers and no shear stress; pressure is the main normal stress.

◆ FLUIDS
✓ Liquids and gases are fluids.

◆ Liquids → Have nearly fixed volume but take the shape of their container.

◆ Gases → Have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume and are highly compressible.

✓ Liquids and solids are nearly incompressible compared with gases.

◆ DENSITY (ρ)
✓ Density → Mass per unit volume:
ρ = m/V

✓ SI unit: kg/m³

✓ Density is important in determining whether objects float or sink and affects fluid pressure.

◆ PRESSURE (P)
✓ Pressure → The normal force acting per unit area:
P = F/A

✓ SI unit: pascal (Pa)
1 Pa = 1 N/m²

✓ A smaller area produces greater pressure for the same force.

◆ Applications of fluid statics:
Hydraulic presses
Car jacks
Dams
Water tanks
Floating/submerged objects

title: 3.2 PRESSURE IN FLUIDS AT REST
notes:
✓ A fluid at rest exerts pressure on surfaces in contact with it.

✓ Pressure increases with depth because deeper points support a greater column of fluid.

◆ PRESSURE DUE TO A LIQUID
✓ P = ρgh

◆ Where:
ρ → Fluid density
h → Depth/height of fluid
g → Gravitational acceleration

✓ Pressure at the same depth in the same fluid is equal.

✓ Pressure depends on depth, density and gravity, not on the container's shape.

◆ ATMOSPHERIC PRESSURE
✓ Atmospheric pressure → The pressure exerted by Earth's atmosphere.

✓ Standard atmospheric pressure:
1 atm = 760 mmHg = 760 torr ≈ 101.3 kPa

◆ GAUGE PRESSURE
✓ Pressure measured relative to atmospheric pressure:
Pgauge = Pabsolute − Patm

◆ ABSOLUTE PRESSURE
✓ Total pressure relative to a perfect vacuum:
Pabsolute = Patm + Pgauge

◆ PASCAL'S LAW
✓ A pressure change applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to all parts of the fluid and the walls of its container.

◆ HYDRAULIC SYSTEM
✓ Hydraulic machines use Pascal's law to transmit and multiply forces.

F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂

◆ PRESSURE-MEASURING DEVICES
Manometer → Measures pressure using liquid columns.
Mercury barometer → Measures atmospheric pressure.

✓ Key idea: Pressure in a stationary fluid acts normally to surfaces.

title: 3.3 ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE
notes:
✓ When an object is placed in a fluid, the fluid exerts an upward force called buoyant force.

✓ This occurs because fluid pressure is greater at greater depth.

◆ BUOYANT FORCE (Fᵦ)
✓ Buoyant force → The net upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object.

◆ ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE
✓ The buoyant force on an object equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

Fᵦ = ρfluidVdisplacedg

◆ FLOATING AND SINKING
✓ Fᵦ > W → Object rises.
✓ Fᵦ < W → Object sinks.
✓ Fᵦ = W → Object remains suspended or floats in equilibrium.

✓ An object floats when its average density is less than the density of the fluid.

◆ SPECIFIC GRAVITY
✓ Specific gravity → Compares the density of a substance with the density of a reference fluid, usually water:

SG = ρobject/ρwater

✓ It has no unit.

◆ APPLICATIONS
Archimedes' principle is used in ships, submarines, hydrometers and determining the density of irregular objects.

✓ Apparent weight in a fluid is reduced because the buoyant force acts upward.

title: 3.4 FLUID FLOW
notes:
✓ Fluid flow occurs because of pressure differences.

✓ A fluid generally moves from a region of higher pressure toward a region of lower pressure.

◆ Examples:
Wind
Blood circulation
Water flowing through pipes

◆ STEADY FLOW
✓ Each fluid particle follows a smooth path, and particles arriving at the same point have the same velocity.

✓ Streamlines do not cross.

◆ TURBULENT FLOW
✓ Irregular and disorderly flow containing whirlpool-like regions.

✓ It commonly occurs at high fluid speeds.

◆ VISCOSITY
✓ Viscosity → The internal friction between adjacent layers of a moving fluid.

✓ It opposes relative motion and converts some kinetic energy into internal energy.

◆ FLOW RATE (Q)
✓ Flow rate → The volume of fluid passing through a cross-section per unit time:
Q = V/t

✓ For a fluid moving through a pipe:
Q = Av

◆ Where:
A → Cross-sectional area
v → Average fluid velocity

◆ EQUATION OF CONTINUITY
✓ For steady flow of an incompressible fluid:
A₁v₁ = A₂v₂

✓ Therefore, when a pipe becomes narrower, the fluid moves faster.

✓ If A₂ < A₁ → v₂ > v₁

◆ BERNOULLI'S PRINCIPLE
✓ As the speed of a moving fluid increases, the pressure it exerts on a surface decreases.

✓ P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant

◆ Where:
p → Pressure
ρ → Fluid density
v → Fluid velocity
g → Acceleration due to gravity
h → Height above a reference level

✓ P₁ + ½ρv₁² + ρgh₁ = P₂ + ½ρv₂² + ρgh₂

✓ This principle helps explain effects such as airflow over an airplane wing, pressure changes in pipes and some biological fluid-flow phenomena.

◆ Applications:
Blood flow
Water pipes
Airflow
Airplane wings
Spray devices
Wind and atmospheric flow

title: 3.5 SAFETY AND HIGH PRESSURE
notes:
✓ High pressure → Pressure much greater than atmospheric pressure; the textbook generally considers pressures above about 50 atm as high pressure.

◆ HIGH-PRESSURE APPLICATIONS
Pressure cookers
Gas cylinders
Tire inflators
High-pressure washers
Industrial and laboratory systems
Food preservation by pascalization

◆ HIGH-PRESSURE EQUIPMENT
Compressors/pumps
High-pressure pipes, fittings and valves
Pressure vessels
Steam generators
Safety valves
Bursting discs
Pressure instruments

◆ COMPRESSOR
✓ A mechanical device that increases gas pressure, commonly by reducing its volume.

◆ PASCALIZATION
✓ Using very high pressure to reduce or eliminate microorganism activity in food, helping extend the shelf life of products such as juice, fish, meat and dairy products.

◆ SAFETY MEASURES
Wear safety glasses/goggles.
Wear gloves and enclosed shoes.
Use appropriate protective equipment.
Never point a pressure washer at people or animals.
Maintain proper working position.
Turn off the machine and water before removing hoses.
Handle gas cylinders carefully and prevent accidental leakage.

✓ High-pressure systems can be extremely useful but can cause serious injury if improperly designed or operated.
